Based on their [[A-League 2007–08|2007–08]] performances, the [[Central Coast Mariners FC|Central Coast Mariners]] and the [[Newcastle Jets FC|Newcastle Jets]] competed in the [[AFC Champions League 2009|2009 AFC Champions League]] for the first time. Changes to the league included: * The introduction of both a [[A-league National Youth League|youth league]] and [[W-League (Australia)|women's league]] aligned with A-League clubs.{{Cite news |date=19 January 2007 |title=FFA: A-League WILL Get Bigger |url=http://au.fourfourtwo.com/news/68598,ffa-aleague-will-get-bigger.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140106010917/http://au.fourfourtwo.com/news/68598,ffa-aleague-will-get-bigger.aspx |archive-date=6 January 2014 |access-date=17 February 2008 |publisher=[[FourFourTwo (Australia)|FourFourTwo]]}} * An increase in the [[salary cap]] to A$1.9 million.{{Cite news |date=2 May 2008 |title=New season to start with a bang sea |url=http://au.fourfourtwo.com/news/75151,new-season-to-start-with-a-bang.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080503031516/http://au.fourfourtwo.com/news/75151%2Cnew-season-to-start-with-a-bang.aspx |archive-date=3 May 2008 |access-date=2 May 2008 |publisher=AU FourFourTwo |df=dmy}} * The addition of a Junior Marquee player. {{flagicon|AUS}} [[Richard Johnson (footballer)|Richard Johnson]] |} == Pre-season Challenge Cup == {{main|2008 A-League Pre-Season Challenge Cup}} All A-League clubs played the pre-season cup competition held in July and August, and were drawn into two groups. Group A consisted of [[Adelaide United FC|Adelaide United]], [[Melbourne Victory FC|Melbourne Victory]], [[Newcastle Jets FC|Newcastle Jets]] and [[Perth Glory FC|Perth Glory]]. Group B was [[Central Coast Mariners FC|Central Coast Mariners]], [[Brisbane Roar FC|Queensland Roar]], [[Sydney FC]] and [[Wellington Phoenix FC|Wellington Phoenix]]. The winner of each group, [[Melbourne Victory FC|Melbourne Victory]] and [[Wellington Phoenix FC|Wellington Phoenix]], met in [[Wellington]] on 6 August 2008 for the Pre-Season Cup Final.[http://www.a-league.com.au/site/_content/document/00000680-source.pdf 2008 Pre-Season Cup Draw] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110518042209/http://www.a-league.com.au/site/_content/document/00000680-source.pdf |date=18 May 2011 }}, Football Federation Australia, 2 May 2008 With the score at 0–0 after 90 minutes, the game went to penalties, [[Melbourne Victory FC|Melbourne Victory]] eventually prevailing 8–7, thus becoming the first team in A-League history to claim all three
